intro: Long before Samsun there was Amisus, an ancient city in Samsun province, from the 7th century BC to the 4th century AD. It was a Black Sea port city, and it left behind tumuli and underground tombs.
history: Milesians founded the city in the 7th century BC. It grew into a major port of Pontus, and under Rome it gained free-city status. Then, in 1995, came a remarkable find: royal tombs on Amisos Hill.
structure-1: You are now at the Amisos Tumuli, royal burial mounds of the Pontic period on Amisos Hill.
structure-2: Here are the underground tombs: burial chambers cut into the rock, hidden below the ground.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the ancient harbour, the rock-cut tombs and the city walls.
facts: Did you know? Gold jewellery from the royal tombs found at Amisos in 1995 is displayed in the Samsun Museum. This Hellenistic gold jewellery from the tumuli is the most striking evidence of wealth on this coast. The city was also one of Mithridates' principal ports, and it was burned during the resistance to Rome.
outro: This brings our tour of Amisus to an end. Please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. Thank you for listening, and enjoy your visit.
